batch_strategy: Use targeted condition contrasts where recent measurements exposed incorrect transfer, complete a crossed loading-volume experiment, and add structural anchors for uncovered neutral families. Reduce further sampling of already well-covered nitrogen response curves while retaining specific unresolved nitrogen and donor probes. All selections use the supplied premeasurement predictions frozen with this packet.

choices.reason: m212 at 1/1 and 150 uL anchors a matched-loading comparison with the selected 10/1 point. Its predicted onset is later than at 5/1, while observed d5234e966aa231be05e5 gives only 7.24/13.67 mL at 5/1 and lower loading. This tests a sparsely labeled secondary-amine response without assuming aromatic-base behavior transfers.

m212 at 10/1 and 150 uL predicts 22.32/39.66 mL and has high CW distance. Together with the selected same-loading 1/1 point and observed d5234e966aa231be05e5, it tests whether this secondary amine develops a weak-eluent retention transition or receives an inappropriate nitrogen-family correction.

Complete the m202 10/1 loading series at 150 uL. Observed 7de812bda21b4dfe46dc at 50 uL is 14.79/21.41 mL, whereas 902937db42f82f467718 at 100 uL is 35.08/70.35 mL. The current 23.52/43.52 prediction makes this a direct discriminator between a reproducible amount response and a localized exceptional observation.

m200 at 2/1 and 150 uL directly contrasts with the 50 uL measurement a92f7617b135de150588. The predictor transfers nearly the same late endpoints across loading. This label tests whether the sparse nitro-alcohol series follows the onset shifts seen in other donor aromatics while retaining its broad completion interval.

m205 at 5/1 extends its measured 1/1 and 2/1 sequence in 2b10c90b32f970e4b4c8 and c973d4c257be9ef08216. The predicted 34.76/70.22 mL tests whether the fused phenethyl alcohol continues a steep response, informed by the newly very late hydroxymethyl analogue b7cf293311f83700cd9a. Their loading conditions differ, so this tests joint transfer.

m206 at 5/1 and 100 uL adds an amount contrast to cdf40bcb3f4392f8d7d1 at 150 uL. After b7cf293311f83700cd9a revealed a much larger 10/1 response, this intermediate label helps distinguish a ratio-specific transition from an amount-dependent shift already present at 5/1.

Measure m125 at 2/1, 100 uL, and 300 uL DCM. Existing 69b09343d0b9995c3ae4 uses the same sample amount with 500 uL DCM and finishes at 56.86 mL; 19f19f196ba5787a01b0 uses 150 uL sample with 300 uL DCM and finishes at 31.38 mL. This fills one missing corner of a crossed design.

Measure the reciprocal m125 corner: 2/1, 150 uL sample, and 500 uL DCM. Together with the other selected corner, 69b09343d0b9995c3ae4, and 19f19f196ba5787a01b0, it separates loading-volume and sample-amount associations from run variability. The model currently predicts almost identical endpoints for these contrasts.

m92 at 1/1 and 150 uL extends the exact-ratio amount series: 00a89de0e6cc7377a84b at 50 uL measured 5.18/12.01 mL and e93e08d6bc42e91e2679 at 100 uL measured 10.24/25.15 mL. The current nearly amount-invariant prediction tests whether the increase continues or the middle point is exceptional.

m92 at 2/1 and 50 uL connects the measured low-loading 1/1 point 00a89de0e6cc7377a84b to later-ratio observations. Alongside the selected 1/1 high-loading point, it helps distinguish ratio response from loading effects in an alpha-ketoester whose repeated 5/1 records also show substantial V2 variation.

m45 at 1/1 and 50 uL tests the early part of the acid curve after 5cc67d02b8fad1c648d6 and 9409394cdc0bcfb31fbc rejected much later predicted completion volumes at 5/1 and 10/1. Its current V2 prediction is already about as large as the measured 5/1 value, making the selected 1/1–2/1 pair informative about local response shape.

m45 at 2/1 and 50 uL forms a fixed-loading ratio contrast with the selected 1/1 experiment and measured 5/1 row 5cc67d02b8fad1c648d6. It tests the model's predicted decrease in V2 between 1/1 and 2/1 without imposing monotonicity on an acid family with irregular recorded behavior.

m211 at 20/1 and 100 uL tests loading transfer from 434e465cfa7e0034f233 at 50 uL. Recent dd4829f39cdf781ffaf9 was overpredicted at 10/1, while 0f06772820e6693753e3 was underpredicted at 50/1 and high loading. This intermediate point localizes the change in completion scaling.

Measure the actual low-loading m216 0/1 anchor. The observed table identifies bae5bd53214695aed5b8 as m187, so that recent outcome cannot establish this quinoline baseline. Comparison with measured ae187d6f3746213b630c and eb56f25c331ea1ab9b2b tests loading effects under pure EA.

m95 at 5/1 and 100 uL fills the interval between measured 2/1, 10/1, and 50/1 conditions. The long completion volumes in 1a55639d058c08a1a06e and 5fd0921bbbba1e22abf9 need a lower-ratio anchor to locate tail development rather than propagate a high-ratio correction throughout the curve.

m82 at 5/1 and 50 uL supplies a missing lower-ratio anchor before its measured 10/1 and 20/1 tails in b6ffd4ffa7739deb3e88 and b6bf451b4911ee22d4a4. Comparison with the selected methyl beta-ketoester m95 tests joint ester-substituent and loading-condition transfer; loading solvent volumes differ.

m166 at 50/1 probes the model's strongly widening extrapolation beyond measured 80de1b57c56257d2ecae at 20/1 and ea9ef1bc8766196ca96d at 10/1. Its broad quantile spreads and maximal CW distance are secondary evidence for testing whether onset remains early while completion grows, or both endpoints move later.

m167 at 50/1 provides the phenyl counterpart to the selected fused-aromatic CF3 diketone. Its predicted 7.05/19.94 mL differs substantially from m166, although measured lower-ratio diketone endpoints are relatively close. This tests whether the structural divergence at weak eluent is real; the selected amounts differ and will be modeled explicitly.

m86 at 2/1 and 100 uL locates the transition before its measured 5/1 response in 9bc73e0c27d4d6b44abb. Together with the selected ortho-aminoester and measured meta-aminoester ca6feb29f6758377a65f, it tests how positional structure and recorded loading conditions jointly determine the early response.

m89 at 2/1 and 100 uL tests the low-retention branch suggested by its 5/1 observations 1cee9fb4b0731101f3a6 and 3aed7873d2fd1cf48684. The selected para-aminoester and observed meta analogue supply a useful positional comparison, while their differing loading solvent conditions remain explicit covariates.

First label for tetralone m180 at 20/1 tests transfer from the closely related seven-membered ketone b8b8becd233748ccae9e3 and methyl-substituted fused ketone f9bba2e75f16ebadb0eb. High structural similarity makes this a focused test of ring-size encoding and condition transfer within a common carbonyl family.

First label for m171 at 20/1 covers a diaryl ketone with a methylene separating one aromatic ring from the carbonyl. Observed m172 in b54f29a73518aa1f30a7 is unavailable as measured evidence, so the relevant measured anchors are f2f54282835725ea01b1 and 9e46469e7c9719ba3611, plus benzophenone-family rows. This tests graph-topology transfer beyond carbonyl counts.

First label for biphenyl aldehyde m189 at 20/1 distinguishes an extended aromatic aldehyde from fused aldehyde m195 and biphenyl ketone m68. Measured cb534927304d5c892100 and the m195 series provide different retention associations despite similar aromatic size, making this useful for learning accessible carbonyl environment.

First label for ortho-tolualdehyde m145 at 50/1 tests positional transfer from meta-tolualdehyde 195a292d7c8874415285 and substituted aldehyde f73fd2f4c55177304721. Steric shielding of the aldehyde is a chemical prior, not an observed effect here; this label checks whether the graph model represents the distinction.

First label for tert-butyl bromopropionate m46 at 50/1 tests its unusually small predicted completion volume, 7.13 mL. Related bromoesters in b9c474ef8c8affc54498 and d86448c8f5aaa8ebcf7f finish substantially later under comparable weak eluent. This can teach how ester sterics and alpha substitution modify transfer.

First label for para-tert-butyl methyl benzoate m100 at 50/1 extends a well-populated ester family into an unseen bulky substituent. Measured 18eb8ff2b9699bbdb4f1 and fc911fe23a3e1e8e87d2 is prediction-only, so use measured c98657e16e93ef4ede6b only if observed; the supplied measured ester anchors are 18eb8ff2b9699bbdb4f1 and ede97e1f4b6e7fe9a7eb. This tests structural transfer at weak eluent.

m193 at 20/1 extends the measured 5/1 and 10/1 nitro-aldehyde sequence in 6ae922f63e983b14e320 and df6457ca86c98c073bf6. Its predicted 42.74/85.90 mL tests a steep extrapolation against the late nitro-acetophenone measurements b6f1b33a5491968c645e and 606886b17304ec494aa0.

m191 at 10/1 predicts a large onset increase relative to 5/1. With the selected same-loading 5/1 point and measured 53becf1a41d72abcc45a at 2/1 and higher loading, it tests whether two aldehydes produce a genuine response transition or an unsupported nonlinear model extrapolation.

m191 at 5/1 and 100 uL anchors the selected 10/1 comparison. Both endpoints are needed to test the predicted onset jump from roughly 7.46 to 22.76 mL while completion increases more moderately, improving learning of onset/completion coupling for a sparsely measured dialdehyde.

m209 at 20/1 and 50 uL completes an amount contrast with bd3435c0f9b14ec7997d and 29b39881584c4fec1c58. Those rows have similar V2 but different onsets, while 80f546c47198fa7c6dbf establishes a later 50/1 tail. This tests loading-sensitive onset separately from completion in a phenolic donor.

First label for dimethyl iodoarene m139 at 2/1 checks the relatively high predicted 7.82/12.66 mL in a nonpolar structure with low similarity to labeled graphs. Measured de3b76c31de84a3a4721 and b9529a88ac5b822de9c4 provide limited iodoarene anchors. This tests whether substitution changes are being overinterpreted across the many early-eluting rows.

First label for isoamyl benzoate m55 at 20/1 tests transfer from the one-carbon-shorter ester m56, whose measured conditions include cb839ce268b9ea4fa20b only as a candidate, so measured anchors are 19e665b6098744dfb60c and 8e175dc1200d398d3489. It extends a common neutral ester relationship with a controlled structural change and recorded loading conditions.

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen-containing molecules require environment-specific ratio responses. A common late-volume correction is inadequate: aromatic systems differ in response curvature and loading dependence, and transfer to the sparsely labeled secondary amine m212 remains untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Recent errors have opposite signs across nitrogen structures and ratios. Selected response anchors can improve graph-condition interactions while avoiding unnecessary repetition of well-covered m90 conditions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m212 follow the predicted nonmonotonic low-ratio branch and later 10/1 transition, and does m211's intermediate-ratio completion response transfer across amount?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl topology determines whether weaker eluent delays onset, broadens the completion interval, or moves both endpoints. Beta-ketoesters, CF3 diketones, and nitro carbonyls should not inherit a uniform tail correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These families contain large historical errors and distinct onset/completion associations. Intermediate conditions and related-structure extrapolations can teach when large V2 changes are family-specific.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where do the m95/m82 tails begin, does the m166/m167 divergence persist at 50/1, and are the predicted m191 and m193 transitions supported by labels?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount and loading solvent volume can interact with structure and ratio, but some recorded endpoint variation may also reflect unrecorded variability. Near-invariant model predictions should be tested with crossed conditions rather than treating every observed difference as a causal amount effect.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The m125 crossed design directly separates recorded amount and solvent-volume associations. m92 includes differing labels for an identical recorded tuple, and m202 has a large amount contrast; these caution against learning a universal loading direction or fitting all scatter deterministically.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the missing m125 corners reproduce a solvent-volume association, and do the new m92 and m202 amount levels follow smooth responses or identify exceptional middle observations?

hypotheses.content: The bromopropionic-acid response is ratio-local. Its measured 5/1–20/1 curve does not support extending a broad late-completion correction to every stronger-eluent condition; the current predicted 1/1-to-2/1 V2 reversal remains untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Recent acid labels exposed large overprediction after earlier severe underprediction. Fixed-loading lower-ratio measurements can localize the response instead of propagating corrections from isolated endpoints.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 50 uL, does completion decrease from 1/1 to 2/1 as predicted, or does the measured curve connect differently to the short 5/1 interval?

hypotheses.content: Donor-containing aromatic molecules can show steep weak-eluent transitions whose location depends on topology. Loading may shift onset more strongly than completion in some series, but transfer among hydroxymethyl, phenethyl, nitro-alcohol, and phenolic environments remains incomplete.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest m206 result exposed a large remaining failure while other donor series were overpredicted. Structure-specific transition anchors and amount contrasts can improve transfer across a broad donor-containing region.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m205 continue its steep response at 5/1, and do new m206, m200, and m209 amount points preserve completion while changing onset?

hypotheses.content: Aminoester retention depends on substitution geometry together with recorded loading conditions. The relatively short ortho-aminoester intervals and longer meta/para intervals suggest a topology-dependent response; intramolecular donor-acceptor interaction is a plausible but unverified explanation.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These structures share coarse descriptors but differ in graph arrangement. Lower-ratio labels can test whether the positional association persists before large tails develop, while explicitly retaining loading solvent and volume differences.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 2/1, do the selected para and ortho aminoesters retain distinct response branches relative to the measured meta analogue?

feedback_interpretation: Recent acquisition errors weaken the idea of a persistent universal nitrogen underprediction: m90 at 5/1 was relatively close in b51b5dbcd2a38b174973 and 855832bd4005ac7abdc6, and m216 at 1/1 and 2/1 was close in d1e71a8278523e7a10e3 and 07933c8c797c30bb0e8e. m211 instead changed error sign between dd4829f39cdf781ffaf9 and 0f06772820e6693753e3. I therefore reduce additional dense sampling of familiar nitrogen curves. The large V2 underprediction for m206 in b7cf293311f83700cd9a strengthens donor-transition questions, while m11, m45, and low-loading m202 outcomes show that corrections from late endpoints can overpropagate. The m202 amount contrast and conflicting repeated m92 records increase the value of distinguishing recorded condition effects from variability. I follow the observed table for identity: bae5bd53214695aed5b8 is m187, not m216, and cannot establish a low-loading quinoline baseline. I also correct earlier solvent-strength wording: increasing PE/EA reduces the EA fraction and weakens the normal-phase eluent; 0/1 is pure EA. Historical errors cited here are acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The batch combines local failure repair with tests of relationships that can transfer across many rows. The crossed m125 experiment is especially informative because it resolves two confounded recorded variables using existing measurements and two missing corners. m92 and m202 amount extensions test whether large observed differences are reproducible response structure or exceptional observations. Fixed-loading m212, m45, and m191 comparisons discriminate specific predicted curve shapes, while m205, m206, m200, and m209 probe donor-dependent transitions and onset/completion coupling. Carbonyl-family bridges and paired diketone extrapolations examine where broad tails emerge. Eight first-molecule anchors test focused structural changes in common neutral families, including ring size, carbonyl connectivity, substitution position, ester sterics, and alkyl-chain extension. Quantile spreads and CW distances serve as secondary model-sensitivity evidence, without being treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty. Together, these labels should improve the retrained model's structure-condition transfer and reduce both underprediction and overprediction across the Row-distribution.
